observation.visible_scene: A dark silhouette of a cargo-style ship (hull, central superstructure, and thin masts/funnels) rests on a choppy deep-blue sea in the lower third of the frame. Behind and above the ship, several enormous pale billowing masses of vapor/spray rise against a hazy blue-gray sky, filling most of the upper frame. The ship and the waterline stay at the same position throughout.
visible_changes: The vapor/spray masses behind the ship expand and rise upward over the excerpt: the rounded billows on the left and center gradually stretch vertically and become more diffuse.
The right-side plume, initially a rounded billow, elongates into a tall rising column that grows higher in later frames.
The overall plume structure climbs toward the top of the frame, indicating continued upward growth rather than a new onset within this segment.
The ship silhouette, the sea horizon, and the sky remain fixed in frame, so the apparent change is expansion/deformation of the plumes, not translation of the vessel or a camera move.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the plumes (volcanic eruption, large breaking waves, steam venting, etc.) is not established by the frames.
The beginning and completion of the plume activity lie outside this crop; the rising is already underway at frame 1 and continues past the last frame.
Whether the ship is drifting or anchored cannot be determined from the static framing.
uncertain_details: Material identity of the billowing masses (steam, smoke, or water spray) is not visually certain.
Any very slow lateral motion of the ship is below the resolution of frame-to-frame comparison and cannot be confirmed.
